meta.basis: 100 synthetic domain validation cases rewritten from internet research on inspection-related contract workflows, deadlines, written amendment requirements, and attorney-review practices. The cases are not copied from source text and are designed to stress state-specific workflow handling rather than repair-cost estimation.
meta.warning: Synthetic validation cases only; not legal advice, broker supervision, lending advice, or verified customer interviews.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC and TRERC guidance: Texas inspection leverage depends on a live option period and written notice or amendment workflow.
cases.deal: Option period expires at 5 p.m. today and the seller has not answered the repair request.
expectedLeadScope: same-day terminate or signed amendment decision
cases.requiredGate: Texas option-period alive and written decision before deadline
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may assume negotiation is still protective after the unrestricted termination window closes.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC FAQ: option fee timing and stated amount can affect whether the Texas unrestricted termination right exists.
cases.deal: Contract says option period, but the file shows no option fee receipt and the inspection found major issues.
cases.requiredGate: confirm option consideration before treating termination right as available
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet may tell the agent to exercise leverage the buyer may not actually have.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC amendment form research: repair agreements should be captured as contract changes, not left in email threads.
cases.deal: Seller texted that they will give a credit, but no amendment is signed and the option period ends tomorrow.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer relies on a side promise that does not show up in the contract file.

cases.sourceBasis: TRERC option-period discussion: inspections can occur without an option period, but termination leverage changes materially.
cases.deal: Buyer waived option period to win a multiple-offer deal and now wants repairs after inspection.
findings: no option period in executed contract
cases.riskIfWrong: Product frames the request like a normal option-period ask and overstates buyer leverage.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC amendment workflow: extending a Texas option period needs proper written handling, not an informal promise.
cases.persona: Team lead reviewing a junior agent
cases.deal: Sewer scope cannot happen until after the option deadline unless the parties extend in writing.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer spends money on a late scope after losing the clean walk-away path.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC materials distinguish inspection negotiation from lender-required repair allocation.
cases.persona: Loan officer and buyer agent pair
cases.deal: FHA appraisal may require repairs while buyer also wants an option-period credit.
cases.requiredGate: separate inspection ask from financing-required repair path
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet may negotiate a credit that cannot cure a lender-visible closing condition.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC option-period guidance: buyer must deliver written termination during the option period when choosing to walk away.
cases.deal: Buyer says they want to cancel but has only told their agent by phone with two hours left.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may miss the deadline because the product treats intent as effective notice.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC/TAR-style repair negotiation relies on contract amendment after seller counter, not a revised informal wishlist.
cases.deal: Seller countered with a small credit and refused repairs; option period still open until tomorrow.
cases.requiredGate: counter acceptance, counteroffer, or terminate before option deadline
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may continue negotiating past the window instead of making a contract decision.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas option-period research: an accepted repair agreement still needs clear completion and documentation terms.
cases.deal: Seller agreed to repair roof leak but amendment omits who completes it and when receipts are due.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer closes with an ambiguous seller obligation and weak enforcement posture.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC FAQ and amendment form: negotiated contract changes require broker/legal boundary awareness.
cases.deal: Agent drafted custom legal language about structural warranty after inspection.
findings: seller agrees only to cosmetic patch
cases.riskIfWrong: Product encourages unauthorized or unenforceable drafting instead of a safe contract handoff.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas option-period workflow: seller backup pressure changes negotiation posture but not deadline mechanics.
cases.deal: Listing agent says a backup offer is waiting if buyer asks for too much.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may lose the deal by sending a maximal demand instead of preserving exit leverage.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC option-period guidance: seller non-response before option expiration should trigger buyer decision logic.
cases.deal: Team wants a workflow rule for seller silence on repair asks.
cases.riskIfWrong: Team misses repeat option deadlines because the tool treats open negotiation as safe.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas amendment source: changing price, repairs, closing date, or option terms belongs in the amendment path.
cases.deal: Investor wants a price reduction rather than seller-performed repairs before option expiration.
cases.requiredGate: price reduction amendment and lender impact check
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet drafts repair language when the negotiated term is a price change.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas option-period and amendment research: extension requests should not hide unresolved specialist inspections.
cases.deal: Water well and septic inspections are incomplete on the last option day.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer proceeds without rural system evidence or a preserved walk-away right.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC guidance: repair negotiations during option period must be separated from inspection report sharing and disclosure consequences.
cases.deal: Buyer sent the entire inspection report with broad demands during option period.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller may overreact to a report dump rather than isolate negotiable defects.

cases.sourceBasis: TREC amendment form: an accepted repair credit should be checked against closing-cost and financing mechanics.
cases.deal: Seller offers a large credit instead of repairing roof and electrical items.
expectedExclusions: credit amount accepted without lender review
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer negotiates a concession that cannot be fully used or does not solve required repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas workflow: post-option repair discoveries are not equivalent to option-period inspection leverage.
cases.deal: Option period expired yesterday; buyer now found a new roof leak after heavy rain.
cases.requiredGate: not sendable as first inspection ask after expired option
cases.riskIfWrong: Product tells agent to send a standard request after the strongest deadline has passed.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas option-period guidance: buyer walk-away, seller counter, and amendment signing must be sequenced before deadline.
cases.deal: Seller counter arrives 30 minutes before option deadline and buyer is traveling.
cases.requiredGate: buyer authorization and timed notice workflow
cases.riskIfWrong: Agent may miss authority or timing, exposing the buyer and brokerage.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas TREC form source: amendment terms may address repairs, lender-required repairs, option extension, and closing date differently.
cases.deal: One draft amendment mixes inspection repairs, lender conditions, and closing extension in a single vague paragraph.
cases.riskIfWrong: Parties sign unclear terms that do not match the actual financing and closing problem.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas option-period research: repair request tools should recognize when buyer should walk away rather than optimize an ask.
cases.deal: Engineer says more testing is needed and seller will not extend the option period.
cases.riskIfWrong: Product pushes a repair ask when the buyer needs a binary risk decision before expiration.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado DRE contract: buyer must choose inspection termination or written inspection objection by the applicable deadline.
cases.deal: Inspection termination deadline is today, but buyer is considering an objection instead.
cases.requiredGate: Colorado termination/objection path selected before deadline
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may file the wrong notice and lose the desired walk-away path.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado DRE contract and objection notice: delivering an inspection objection changes the buyer's termination path and starts resolution logic.
cases.deal: Buyer already delivered an Inspection Objection and now wants to terminate before the resolution deadline.
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet drafts the wrong document for a file already in resolution posture.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado objection notice: if written settlement is not reached by resolution deadline, termination risk must be surfaced.
cases.deal: Resolution deadline is tomorrow and seller verbally accepted a sewer credit.
cases.riskIfWrong: Contract may terminate despite everyone believing the sewer credit was agreed.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado DRE form distinguishes inspection report attachment from written description of unsatisfactory conditions.
cases.deal: Agent plans to attach only the full report as the objection.
findings: full inspection report with many comments
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller cannot tell what must be corrected and the objection may fail the workflow need.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado contract: unresolved inspection objection can terminate unless buyer withdraws it before the deadline.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to keep the property even though seller refuses the objection.
cases.requiredGate: withdrawal or written resolution before automatic termination risk
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer unintentionally loses the contract by doing nothing.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado inspection objection workflow: seller counter should be evaluated against the already-delivered objection and resolution deadline.
cases.deal: Seller counters only one of three objected items with 24 hours left.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer signs a partial resolution believing all objected items were handled.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado DRE contract includes broad property-condition concerns, but objection must still be timely and focused.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to object to noise, road project, and roof leak after inspections.
cases.requiredGate: timely written objection for property-condition concerns
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet narrows Colorado objection rights too much or bloats it with cosmetics.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado objection notice: report may or may not be provided, but the product should flag disclosure and strategy consequences.
cases.deal: Buyer provided an objection but withheld the inspection report.
expectedExclusions: demand for entire report without strategy review
cases.requiredGate: report attachment and disclosure strategy check
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller-side response may be underinformed or create avoidable disclosure friction.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado contract: buyer-paid inspections and damage/liens from invasive testing need workflow guardrails.
cases.deal: Buyer wants destructive mold testing before the inspection deadline.
findings: seller has not authorized invasive testing
cases.requiredGate: inspection access and damage responsibility check
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer creates a property-damage dispute while trying to preserve inspection rights.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado resolution workflow: negotiated repairs can alter contract terms and should be handled as formal resolution.
cases.deal: Seller and buyer agree to extend closing and perform repairs after resolution talks.
findings: resolution draft only says seller to handle
cases.requiredGate: inspection resolution and contract-term change review
cases.riskIfWrong: Repair obligations and closing timing are not actually aligned in the contract.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado contract: buyer's right to terminate under inspection termination expires once an objection is delivered.
cases.deal: Agent sent an objection yesterday, then buyer asks to use inspection termination today.
expectedExclusions: inspection termination as if no objection was sent
cases.riskIfWrong: Product invokes a termination route that may no longer be available.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado objection/resolution deadlines should drive whether to ask, counter, withdraw, or walk away.
cases.deal: Remote buyer is unavailable on the resolution deadline because of travel.
cases.requiredGate: client decision and written resolution timing
cases.riskIfWrong: Agent cannot get authority in time and the contract outcome is accidental.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado inspection objection notice centers unsatisfactory conditions the buyer requires seller to correct.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a price reduction but the objection draft reads like a repair list.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller focuses on performing repairs when buyer's actual acceptable outcome is economic.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado DRE contract: deadlines around disclosures and inspection objections are separate but can interact.
cases.deal: Seller property disclosure arrived late after buyer already objected.
findings: late seller disclosure reveals prior basement flooding
existing objection covers sump pump failure
cases.requiredGate: Colorado disclosure and objection timeline check
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may resolve known items without addressing a newly disclosed material issue.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado resolution workflow: mutual termination can be separate from waiting for resolution deadline.
cases.deal: Both sides want to end the deal after inspection without waiting for the resolution deadline.
expectedExclusions: waiting by default without release review
cases.riskIfWrong: File sits in limbo while earnest money and relisting timing remain unresolved.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado inspection workflow: objection deadlines do not excuse vague asks unsupported by specialist evidence.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to demand a full foundation rebuild before engineer review.
expectedExclusions: full rebuild demand without engineer scope
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller dismisses the objection as exaggerated and no extension is secured.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado objection notice requires buyer signature and deadline-aware written handling.
cases.deal: Agent prepared the objection but buyer has not signed before the evening deadline.
cases.riskIfWrong: The team believes the objection is preserved when it was never properly delivered.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado inspection resolution: withdrawal keeps the contract alive but can waive the objection leverage.
cases.deal: Buyer considers withdrawing objection to avoid termination, but roof issue remains unresolved.
findings: buyer fears losing low interest rate
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer keeps the deal but loses negotiation leverage without understanding the exposure.

cases.sourceBasis: C.A.R.-style California workflow: buyer investigation, repair request, contingency removal, and cancellation are sequenced in writing.
cases.deal: Investigation contingency deadline is tomorrow and seller has not responded to a Request for Repair.
cases.requiredGate: California RR response not treated as automatic contingency removal
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may wait for a seller response and miss the contingency decision point.

cases.sourceBasis: California sources: seller may be asked for repairs, but no response or refusal generally leaves buyer with contingency choices.
cases.deal: Seller refuses all repairs but buyer still has the investigation contingency.
cases.requiredGate: buyer contingency choice after seller refusal
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet implies the seller owes repairs merely because the request was sent.

cases.sourceBasis: California contingency-removal research: contingencies are not safely treated as gone unless the required written removal occurs.
cases.deal: Inspection contingency date passed, but buyer has not signed contingency removal.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller assumes buyer is locked in and fails to use the proper cure/cancellation workflow.

cases.sourceBasis: California request-for-repair guidance: repair requests should be specific and supported, not every inspection comment.
cases.deal: Agent drafted a Request for Repair using every summary item from the inspection report.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller rejects a valid safety request because it is packaged as a cosmetic punch list.

cases.sourceBasis: California form research: repair agreement can be tied to contingency removal, so the sequence must be explicit.
cases.deal: Seller agreed to a credit, but buyer has not decided whether to remove the investigation contingency.
expectedLeadScope: credit agreement and contingency removal sequence
cases.riskIfWrong: File treats economic agreement and contingency waiver as the same event when they are not.

cases.sourceBasis: California investigation contingency source: seller documents delivered late can alter review timing in form-driven workflows.
cases.deal: HOA documents arrive after buyer already removed physical inspection contingency.
findings: late HOA minutes disclose balcony litigation
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may invoke the wrong contingency and lose a valid document-review issue.

cases.sourceBasis: California request-for-repair guidance: seller credit should be checked against lender and closing-cost use limits.
cases.deal: Seller offers a credit larger than buyer's remaining closing costs.
findings: buyer has low remaining closing costs
expectedExclusions: credit amount accepted without lender review
cases.requiredGate: lender and escrow credit check before RR response
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer negotiates money they cannot actually receive or apply.

cases.sourceBasis: California investigation source: buyer inspections generally need access and cannot assume destructive testing without authorization.
cases.deal: Mold contractor wants to cut drywall during inspection period.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer creates a breach or damage dispute while investigating the defect.

cases.sourceBasis: California contingency-removal research: seller may need to prompt performance rather than assume deadlines self-execute.
cases.deal: Buyer missed the investigation deadline and has not removed contingencies or canceled.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller loses leverage by assuming the buyer's rights disappeared automatically.

cases.sourceBasis: California request-for-repair practice: requests should separate broken systems from upgrades and future remodel preferences.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller to replace aged but working systems before removing contingency.
cases.requiredGate: defect versus upgrade boundary in RR
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer weakens a real safety issue by bundling it with improvement demands.

cases.sourceBasis: California repair request workflow: if buyer cancels, it should be handled as cancellation under remaining contingency, not as another counter.
cases.deal: Seller counters with a small credit and buyer wants to walk away before contingency removal.
cases.requiredGate: active contingency and cancellation form handoff
cases.riskIfWrong: Product continues negotiation when the buyer's intended outcome is termination.

cases.sourceBasis: California RR guidance: request expiration and contingency deadlines are separate timing risks.
cases.deal: Request for Repair expiration is later than the investigation contingency deadline.
findings: Request for Repair expires in three days
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer waits on the RR response and misses the actual contingency deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: California request-for-repair sources: seller-requested repairs and lender/appraisal repairs should not be conflated.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a credit for items that the appraiser may require to be repaired before closing.
cases.requiredGate: lender-visible repair caveat in California RR
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet solves negotiation optics but not loan closing risk.

cases.sourceBasis: California contingency-removal research: buyers who waive inspection contingencies shift the product from request drafting to risk advisory.
cases.deal: Buyer waived investigation contingency to win and now wants credits after reviewing disclosures.
findings: seller disclosure mentions prior roof leak
cases.riskIfWrong: Product tells agent to send a normal RR when buyer may have no contingency leverage.

cases.sourceBasis: California workflow: repair response should preserve broker review when the wording could create legal obligations.
cases.deal: Agent drafted seller warranty language for future sewer failure after a sewer scope.
cases.riskIfWrong: Broker sees the tool as unauthorized legal drafting rather than transaction support.

cases.sourceBasis: California request-for-repair best practice: supporting documentation should be scoped and attached deliberately.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to ask for a roof credit using only a verbal roofer opinion.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller rejects the dollar amount as invented and buyer wastes the contingency window.

cases.sourceBasis: California workflow: removal of some contingencies does not necessarily remove every remaining contingency.
cases.deal: Buyer removed loan contingency but not investigation contingency and now has inspection concerns.
cases.riskIfWrong: Product wrongly blocks a valid inspection response or wrongly says buyer is protected.

cases.sourceBasis: California request-for-repair guidance: buyers should not equate seller pre-list inspections with completing their own investigation.
cases.deal: Buyer relied on seller reports and has two days left to decide whether to inspect independently.
findings: buyer has not done own inspection
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer removes contingency without validating a known moisture risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida Realtors/Florida Bar AS IS contract research: inspection period creates cancellation leverage but not a default seller repair duty.
cases.deal: AS IS inspection period ends tonight and buyer wants seller to repair everything.
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet implies seller is obligated to repair under AS IS rather than framing buyer leverage correctly.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS source: buyer cancellation must be timely and in writing within the inspection period.
cases.deal: Buyer says by phone they want to cancel with one hour left in the inspection period.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may lose deposit protection by failing to deliver proper notice on time.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS workflow: repair request does not automatically extend the inspection period.
cases.deal: Buyer sent a repair request yesterday and thinks the inspection period paused.
cases.requiredGate: AS IS deadline continues unless extended in writing
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer waits for a seller response and loses the clean cancellation right.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS practice: seller may renegotiate, but written addendum is needed for agreed credit or repair terms.
cases.deal: Seller verbally agrees to a credit for electrical repairs during inspection period.
cases.requiredGate: written AS IS addendum or cancellation backup
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer lets the inspection period expire while relying on a non-final concession.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS contract research: buyer may inspect as desired within the period, including insurance-sensitive systems.
cases.deal: Four-point inspection is delayed until after the inspection period.
findings: water heater at end of useful life
cases.requiredGate: insurance inspection complete or written extension
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer closes into an insurance problem that should have been resolved during AS IS due diligence.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS workflow: cancellation leverage is time-limited; post-period repair requests are materially different.
cases.deal: Inspection period expired three days ago and buyer now asks for a roof credit.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller or buyer acts as though the original cancellation right remains open.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: seller repair obligation is limited unless separately agreed, so repair quality needs written specs if accepted.
cases.deal: Seller agrees to fix a plumbing leak before closing but refuses to name a licensed plumber.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer accepts a vague repair promise and discovers poor work at walkthrough.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS practice: buyer can request concessions but should be ready to cancel if seller refuses before the deadline.
cases.deal: Seller says no repairs and no credits with two days left in inspection period.
cases.requiredGate: accept AS IS or timely cancel
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer keeps bargaining until the cancellation window expires.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS contract timing: time calculations and delivery dates matter for notice and contract performance.
cases.deal: Inspection period ends on a weekend and the team is unsure whether the deadline rolls.
cases.riskIfWrong: Notice may be late because the tool guesses deadline treatment.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: condo/shared component issues require responsibility checks before making seller repair demands.
cases.deal: Inspection finds balcony and roof issues in a condo during AS IS period.
findings: balcony waterproofing may be association responsibility
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer asks the wrong party for common-element repairs and misses the cancellation deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: buyer due diligence can include additional inspections, but deadlines should drive specialist scheduling.
cases.deal: Mold assessor cannot return lab results until after the inspection period.
expectedExclusions: waiting for late lab results without extension
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer loses the AS IS exit while waiting for evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: seller disclosure duties and inspection rights are separate from negotiated repairs.
cases.deal: Buyer alleges seller hid a prior roof leak during inspection-period negotiations.
findings: prior roof leak disclosed by neighbor
cases.requiredGate: disclosure concern and AS IS cancellation strategy
cases.riskIfWrong: Product escalates factual allegations without evidence and misses the practical deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: cancellation and release of deposit can be procedurally distinct from repair negotiation.
cases.deal: Buyer timely cancels in inspection period, but seller refuses to sign release.
cases.riskIfWrong: Agent confuses cancellation effectiveness with escrow release mechanics.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: inspection period should be used to decide whether a repair addendum, price change, or cancellation is the right path.
cases.deal: Investor wants a price cut for post-closing cast iron replacement before AS IS period expires.
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet produces repair language instead of the agreed economic term.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: repair negotiations should account for lender and insurance repair requirements in addition to buyer preference.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a credit for roof age, but insurer may require replacement before binding coverage.
expectedExclusions: small credit accepted without insurance clearance
cases.requiredGate: insurance and financing clearance before AS IS deadline
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer accepts a concession and later cannot insure or close.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: sending the whole inspection report is not the same as a signed buyer request or cancellation notice.
cases.deal: Buyer agent forwarded the inspection report with no signed repair request.
cases.riskIfWrong: Listing side treats informal report delivery as a binding repair demand.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS: buyers can walk away during the inspection period, but must avoid post-deadline regret framing.
cases.deal: Buyer is emotionally attached and wants to sleep on a major structural issue until after deadline.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer turns a protected decision into an unprotected post-deadline problem.

cases.sourceBasis: New Jersey consumer guide: contracts prepared by licensees include a three-business-day attorney review clause and verbal counters should be written.
cases.deal: Seller verbally accepted inspection credit during attorney review, but attorney has not approved.
cases.requiredGate: NJ attorney review and written contract modification
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer believes the deal is locked before attorney review and written terms are finalized.

cases.sourceBasis: New Jersey consumer guide: attorney review can modify or nullify a licensee-prepared contract within the review period.
cases.deal: Seller receives a higher backup offer while first contract is in attorney review.
expectedExclusions: treating first contract as fully final
cases.requiredGate: attorney review status before advising parties
cases.riskIfWrong: Agent gives certainty that the contract may not yet have under state practice.

cases.sourceBasis: New Jersey guide: counteroffers may be communicated verbally but should be memorialized and only become binding through contract terms.
cases.deal: Listing agent says seller will fix septic if buyer signs, but the contract draft is silent.
cases.requiredGate: NJ attorney inclusion before relying on repair promise
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer signs a contract that does not contain the septic obligation.

cases.sourceBasis: New Jersey attorney review: inspection timing often follows review completion, so scheduling and deadline assumptions matter.
cases.deal: Buyer scheduled inspection before attorney review concluded and seller attorney disapproved contract.
expectedExclusions: assuming inspection spend means contract survives
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer spends money on inspections for a deal that may be nullified.

cases.sourceBasis: New Jersey consumer guide: attorney review period is business-day based and starts from delivery of completely signed contracts.
cases.deal: Parties disagree whether attorney review ended because fully signed contracts were delivered late Friday.
findings: fully signed contract delivered late Friday
cases.riskIfWrong: Agent may tell buyer the contract is binding or cancellable on the wrong day.

cases.sourceBasis: New Jersey workflow: attorney review modifications can address inspection rights and repair obligations before inspections occur.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to keep inspection right despite seller pushing as-is language in attorney review.
cases.requiredGate: attorney review of as-is and inspection contingency
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may sign away inspection leverage without understanding the rider.

cases.sourceBasis: Chicago REALTORS contract: attorney approval and inspection periods are distinct written-notice workflows.
cases.deal: Attorney approval period and inspection period both expire this week.
cases.requiredGate: Illinois attorney approval and inspection notice clocks
cases.riskIfWrong: Team may satisfy one deadline while missing the other.

cases.sourceBasis: Chicago contract: inspection notice should identify unacceptable defects and include pertinent report pages, not a full cosmetic list.
cases.deal: Agent prepares inspection notice with cosmetic items under a Chicago-area contract.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller attorney rejects the notice as outside the inspection clause's intended scope.

cases.sourceBasis: Chicago contract: if written agreement resolving inspection issues is not reached within the period, termination may be available.
cases.deal: Seller attorney counters after the inspection period expired and no extension was signed.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may think the counter is timely when the contract status is disputed.

cases.sourceBasis: Chicago contract: minor repairs below stated threshold may not constitute covered inspection defects.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for many minor items instead of major component defects.
cases.riskIfWrong: Product overvalidates a request the seller can frame as outside inspection notice scope.

cases.sourceBasis: Illinois attorney approval source: proposed modifications exclude certain economics in the standard attorney modification path.
cases.deal: Buyer asks attorney to use attorney review solely to lower the price after inspection.
expectedLeadScope: proper inspection or attorney modification route
cases.requiredGate: attorney review boundary and inspection notice coordination
cases.riskIfWrong: Agent misroutes an inspection issue into a modification path that may not fit the form.

cases.sourceBasis: Chicago contract: in absence of written inspection notice before expiration, inspection provision can be deemed waived.
cases.deal: Buyer verbally told agent about defects but no inspection notice was sent before deadline.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer believes defects were preserved because they told their agent.

cases.sourceBasis: Chicago contract: attorney modifications and inspection notices are served by notice and should be tracked by delivery.
cases.deal: Attorney emailed inspection objections to the wrong address on the last day.
cases.riskIfWrong: Parties fight over whether the inspection notice was effective.

cases.sourceBasis: New York attorney-market industry pattern: contract terms are typically attorney-negotiated before execution, so pre-contract inspection posture differs from post-contract states.
cases.deal: Buyer inspected before signing and now wants repairs while seller entertains another offer.
cases.requiredGate: NY attorney contract status before repair leverage
cases.riskIfWrong: Product assumes escrow-style protection before a contract exists.

cases.sourceBasis: New York attorney-market workflow: inspection findings often become attorney rider terms before signature.
cases.deal: Attorney wants concise inspection issues for contract rider drafting.
cases.requiredGate: attorney-rider summary, not standalone repair demand
cases.riskIfWrong: Output looks like an agent repair request instead of attorney-ready issue framing.

cases.sourceBasis: Connecticut attorney-market practice: attorney-prepared contracts and contingency language need review before relying on repair rights.
cases.deal: Offer has inspection contingency, but attorney draft narrows remedies to terminate-only.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer asks for seller work when the contract may only allow accept-or-terminate.

cases.sourceBasis: Massachusetts attorney/P&S workflow: inspection contingency terms in the purchase and sale agreement control timing and remedies.
cases.deal: Offer inspection deadline differs from the draft purchase and sale inspection language.
expectedExclusions: choosing favorable date without attorney review
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer misses the enforceable inspection date because the tool picks the wrong document.

cases.sourceBasis: Attorney-review states: agent should summarize defects and options without pretending to provide legal notice.
cases.deal: Attorney asks agent not to send any repair demand directly to seller.
cases.riskIfWrong: Product bypasses counsel and creates unauthorized communication risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Attorney-review workflow: inspection and attorney review can overlap, creating cost and deadline tradeoffs.
cases.deal: Buyer hesitates to pay for sewer scope before attorney approval ends.
expectedLeadScope: inspection spend versus attorney review risk
cases.requiredGate: cost/risk tradeoff before attorney review ends
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer either wastes inspection money or misses the chance to find a major defect.

cases.sourceBasis: Attorney-review states: all modifications and counters should be tracked in writing with counsel when applicable.
cases.deal: Multiple attorney emails changed inspection dates, but the team calendar still uses the original date.
cases.requiredGate: single source of truth for attorney-modified dates
cases.riskIfWrong: Team sends notices early, late, or to the wrong party because the file has competing dates.

cases.sourceBasis: Attorney-market transactions: as-is language does not automatically answer whether inspection cancellation or repair requests survive.
cases.deal: Buyer signed as-is offer with inspection contingency and now asks for safety repairs.
expectedLeadScope: attorney review of as-is and contingency interaction
expectedExclusions: blanket rejection based only on as-is label
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller rejects a request that may still be valid under the negotiated contingency.

cases.sourceBasis: Attorney-review workflows: inspection report sharing may have disclosure and negotiation consequences.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to send entire report to seller attorney before contract signing.
findings: full report includes dozens of minor issues
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer creates friction and disclosure fallout without improving contract terms.

cases.sourceBasis: Attorney-review and inspection workflows: termination after unresolved inspection issues should match contract notice terms.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to terminate after seller rejects inspection notice.
expectedExclusions: casual email saying buyer is out
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer creates an earnest-money dispute by terminating informally.

cases.sourceBasis: Attorney-review states: buyer-agent tools should defer legal interpretation of riders while still prioritizing defect evidence.
